items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: I played some of his arrangements at CBS years ago

ctx.x: I played some of his arrangements at CBS years ago, you know, and he could do it, too, because he conducted the Boston Pops last summer here, and he did his own Ellington medley that he had orchestrated, and he opened -- I couldn't hear it because I had to come to work here, but I did hear the opening number that he did. He orchestrated Bach's 'Toccata and Fugue' in D minor. You ever hear that, Ted? It was done back in the twenties.

But Norman did it and it sounded just like the real thing. But these are men that I know that can write for a big orchestra, because I couldn't -- I'm used to writing for the alto sax and the tenor sax, the trombone and the trumpet. But those guys, they're writing for the English horn, the oboes, and the flutes and the French horns
